lines: The price of bread went up again this week, and the loaves are getting smaller besides.
My neighbour swears she heard digging under her floor last night. I told her it was rats.
Mind the gutter, love. The rain has turned this whole street into a river of muck.
They say another band went down through the Mistgate at dawn. None came up by supper.
I keep a candle in the window for my brother. He went up to the castle and never wrote.
Fine weather for once. Enjoy it, traveller, the mist will roll back in by evening.
Salt from Graymourne costs twice what it did last spring. Fog on the roads, they say.
If you're going down below, bring me back nothing. I want no cursed trinkets in my house.
The well water tastes of iron lately. My husband says it's the dungeon breathing up at us.
I've three children, two goats and one roof that leaks. Some days I envy the goats.
You've the look of someone who sleeps in armour. Come by for soup if you're ever hungry.
Old Marta claims she saw a spider the size of a hay cart creeping along the castle walls.
Everyone on our street is either a widow, a gambler or a fool. I'm told I'm all three.
The baker's lad and the cooper's girl are courting. The whole street knows but their fathers.
Wool is cheap and boots are dear this season. Make of that what you will.
I pray to whatever is listening that the Mistgate stays shut while I sleep.
A pilgrim from Vel Morrath blessed my doorstep. The cat still won't go near it.
Don't buy fish on market day. It's been sitting in the sun since the early morning.
My grandmother remembered when the castle had a lord. Now it only has its ghosts.
Strangers bring coin and trouble in equal measure. Which are you bringing, I wonder?
The chimney sweep found a bone in our flue. Nobody's claimed it, and nobody's asking.
I've swept this step every morning for twenty years. The dust never tires, and neither do I.
Ashenreach sends us nails and soot. I'd trade the lot for one clear blue sky.
If you see the tanner, tell him his stink has reached my washing again.
The night bells rang thrice last week. Nobody will say what came up out of the dark.
We had a good harvest, thank the gods. Now the tax man will be wanting his share.
Heard they pulled a troll's tooth out of the Mistgate stair. Big as my forearm, it was.
You're brave, going where you go. Or mad. My mother always said the two look alike.
The cobbles are slick with frost this morning. I've already fallen twice and cursed thrice.
My son wants to be an adventurer like you. I'd rather he learned to mend shoes.
The chandler charges a copper more for every candle now. Darkness is cheaper, and there's plenty.
Some say the mages of Kethrys Spire could seal the castle for good. They never come, though.
Rain, wind, and the cart wheel broke. Still, nobody's died today, and that counts for something.
Keep your purse close in the crowd. Not every hand here is honest, mine included.
I dared Tomas to touch the castle gate, and he cried before he got halfway!
Are you a real knight? You don't look like the ones in Mama's stories.
There's a monster under the bridge. I saw its eyes, all yellow and blinky.
I'm the dungeon troll and you have to pay me a pebble to pass!
Papa says if I don't do my chores the spiders will come and take my toes.
Can you lift me up on your shoulders? I want to see over the wall!
I found a shiny button. It's my treasure now, so don't you take it.
We're playing heroes and monsters. I always have to be the monster. It's not fair.
My big sister kissed the miller's boy. Ew. Don't tell anyone I told you.
Mama makes me fetch water every morning. The bucket is nearly as heavy as me.
Does it hurt to fight a skeleton? Do their bones go clatter clatter?
I'm not scared of the dark. I just like sleeping with the candle on.
Bet you can't hop on one foot all the way to the well. I can!
When I grow up I'm going down the Mistgate and bringing back a dragon egg.
Granny says the fog in Graymourne eats children who wander off. Is that true?
Shh! We're hiding from Bertram. He's counting to a hundred, but he skips numbers.
My dog chased a rat as big as a cat. Then the rat chased my dog.
I made a sword out of a stick. It's called Bonecrusher. Want to hold it?
Why is your armour all scratched? Did a dragon do it? Was it two dragons?
I can count to fifty and I know all my letters except the squiggly one.
Papa works up at the castle. He says the walls whisper, but I think he's fibbing.
Can I have a copper? I want a honey cake. Just one. Please, please, please?
Lina says a ghost lives in the old well. We dropped a stone and it never splashed.
I'm guarding this door. Nobody passes unless they say the secret word. It's 'turnip'.
I fell in the mud and Mama's going to be so cross. Don't look at me!
Do orcs have mothers? Do their mothers make them eat porridge too?
I caught a frog! His name is Sir Hops, and he's going to be a knight.
The big boys say there's a daemon in the cellar. I'm not going down there, ever.
My tooth is wobbly. Granny says if I lose it, a mouse brings me a copper.
I want to be just like you. Can you teach me to fight? I'm very fast.
We buried a dead bird and said a prayer. Do birds go to the gods too?
I ran all the way round the square nine times. Now I feel a bit sick.
Mama says don't talk to strangers. But you're not a stranger if you tell me your name.
When the bells ring at night, I hide under the blanket and hold my breath.
Keep moving, stranger. No loitering by the gate after the second bell.
Curfew's at dusk. After that, anyone still on the streets answers to me.
Twelve hours on this wall and all I've seen is fog and crows. Lucky me.
If you're bound for the Mistgate, sign the ledger. Somebody ought to know your name after.
I've stood this post nine winters. The cold gets into your bones and never leaves.
State your business. Not that it matters, the captain lets anyone through these days.
Heard scratching under the castle stones last night. I told the sergeant. He laughed at me.
Weapons stay sheathed inside the walls. Draw steel in the market and you'll spend the night in irons.
You'd think the night watch would be quiet. You'd be wrong, and so was I.
A merchant from Ashenreach tried to bribe me with a lump of coal. Coal, of all things.
Something big came up the Mistgate stair last month. We still haven't found all of Harlan.
Keep your eyes open on the north road. Bandits out there, or worse than bandits.
My halberd's older than I am, and it's seen more fighting than I ever will, gods willing.
Don't mind me. I'm just counting faces. I like to know who comes back.
The captain wants extra torches on the walls. Says the dark's been creeping closer.
Pass, traveller. You look too tired to be trouble, and I'm too tired to check.
Refugees at the gate again this morning. We let them in. What else could we do?
If you hear the horn three times, get indoors and bar the door. Don't stop to argue.
Lost two of the watch to a fever, so I'm standing triple shifts. Wonderful.
Mind the drunkards near the tavern. They're harmless, mostly, but they do like to swing.
I'd trade this post for a warm hearth and a quiet wife. Haven't found either yet.
You came out of the castle in one piece? That makes you rarer than an honest tax collector.
A cloaked fellow asked after you yesterday. Didn't give a name. I didn't like his eyes.
The gate shuts at sundown, and it does not open again for anyone until dawn.
Report anything strange to the watch house. Strange as in teeth, claws, or too many legs.
My brother guards the walls of Vel Morrath. He says the dead sleep easier there.
Every dawn I check the bars of the Mistgate. Every dawn they're scored a little deeper.
Stand straight, look sharp, and pray nothing comes over the wall. That's the whole job.
No, you can't climb the watchtower. Yes, everyone asks. No, the view is not worth it.
They pay us in copper and promises. The copper always runs out first.
If you see the captain, I'm wide awake and was never asleep. Understood?
Strangers are welcome here, so long as they leave their trouble outside the walls.
My feet ache, my back aches, and my helmet leaks. Glory, they told me. Glory.
A good guard sees everything and says nothing. I'm a terrible guard, as you can tell.
Two weeks ago I was a cobbler. Now they hand me a spear and call me a soldier.
The sergeant makes us drill at dawn. My arms feel like wet rope by noon.
This helmet was made for a bigger head. It wobbles every time I turn around.
If the monsters come up from below, I'll stand my ground. Probably. I hope.
My wife sewed my name into this tunic, so they'll know who to bring home.
We've got forty pikes and thirty men who know which end is pointy.
I practise lunging at hay sacks. Very brave, the hay sacks. They never flinch.
My little girl cried when I left this morning. I told her I'd be home for supper.
They say we're the last line if the castle falls. Some line we make.
My shield is a barrel lid with a strap. The smith promised a proper one next month.
Left, right, left, right. I've marched so much I dream in footsteps now.
Old Gerran fainted at drill yesterday. He's seventy if he's a day, and they drafted him anyway.
I've never killed anything bigger than a chicken, and I felt bad about the chicken.
When the horn sounds we form up by the well. I've practised running there in my sleep.
The captain says courage is just fear that's said its prayers. I've said a great many.
My crops won't harvest themselves while I'm standing here with a stick and a frown.
I heard the real soldiers laughing at our drill. Let them laugh. We're here, aren't we?
My boots were my father's. He wore them in the last war and came home in them.
They gave us a banner. It's mostly patches now, but it's ours, and we're proud of it.
Is it true what they say about trolls? That only fire stops them knitting back together?
A spear's just a long knife, they told me. I still hold it like a broom.
Night watch makes every shadow look like a goblin. Twice tonight I nearly stabbed a cat.
We drill, we eat, we drill again. Nobody's told us what we're drilling for, exactly.
My mother sends me bread every morning. The other lads are jealous, so I share.
I'd rather be baking than marching, but the bakery won't matter much if the walls fall.
Keep your distance from Pell. He swings that axe like he's angry at the air itself.
My knees knock louder than the drum. The sergeant says at least it keeps time.
Volunteered, they wrote in the ledger. I don't recall volunteering, but there it is in ink.
If you're going below, slay one for us. We'd rather never see one up here.
The real soldiers have mail. We have quilted jerkins and a great deal of hope.
I'm told I'll learn to sleep in a ditch. I'm told a great many things.
Most of us joined because our neighbours did. Shame is a fine recruiter.
My son polishes my spear every night. He thinks I'm a hero. I mustn't disappoint him.
They promised us pay at the end of the season. We'll see if we're alive to collect it.
There's a pit of monsters under our feet, and the sergeant's worried about dust on the bunks.
Rations again: hard bread, harder cheese, and a sausage I wouldn't feed a dog.
I fought at the river crossing twenty years back. Still hear the horns in my sleep.
They rotate us down to the first gate of the dungeon. Nobody likes the rotation.
Saw a man come back from below with his hair gone white. He was twenty-three.
Polish your boots, sharpen your blade, and never volunteer. Best advice I ever got.
The garrison's half what it was. Fever took some, the dungeon took the rest.
A soldier fights for three things: his pay, his mates, and a dry place to sleep.
You're the one who goes down there for coin? Better you than me, and I mean that kindly.
Sergeant says orcs fight in packs. So do we. Difference is, they enjoy it.
My shield arm's been numb since the fight with the ghouls. The surgeon says it'll pass.
We've a wager going on how long the new recruits last. My copper's on the tall one.
There's a draught from the dungeon that comes up through the barracks floor. Smells like graves.
I served in Ashenreach once. Hot as a forge and twice as loud. I miss it.
Never trust a quiet corridor below the castle. Quiet means something's waiting for you.
The quartermaster counts every arrow. Lose one, and it comes out of your pay.
My old captain died with a laugh on his lips. I'd like to go the same way, but much later.
Drill at dawn, watch at dusk, and dice in between. That's a soldier's life.
The undead don't tire, don't bleed and don't run. Makes them the worst sort of enemy.
I write to my mother every week. I don't tell her about the spiders.
They gave me a medal once. Sold it for a cloak the following winter. Better use of it.
Keep your blade oiled down there. The damp in those halls rusts steel overnight.
Old Fenwick says he once wrestled a troll. He's lying, but he lies beautifully.
Ten years in this garrison and I've yet to lay eyes on the lord who pays us.
The cook burned the porridge again. We ate it anyway. Soldiers eat what's put before them.
When the daemon broke through the lower gate, I held the line. Then I ran. Then I held it again.
If the sergeant asks, I'm on latrine duty. If anyone else asks, I'm asleep.
Every soldier's got a scar story. Mine's from a goose. Don't you dare laugh.
I've marched from Graymourne to the eastern hills and back. My feet will never forgive me.
Fear is good. Fear keeps you awake. It's the ones who aren't afraid we end up burying.
The new mail shirts came from the forge city. Lighter, stronger, and they still pinch.
Bring back a trophy from below and you'll drink free in the barracks for a month.
My mate swore he heard singing behind the dungeon's third door. Nobody sings down there. Nobody living.
We stand between the dark and these streets. Not much of a wall, but a stubborn one.
We walked six days from the river villages. My shoes gave out on the fourth.
Our farm burned in one night. I didn't even have time to save the cat.
They let us in at the gate, thank the gods. Out there, the roads aren't safe anymore.
My children ask when we're going home. I haven't the heart to tell them there is no home.
Could you spare a crust? Not for me. My little one hasn't eaten since yesterday.
We had a mill, a cow and a good roof. Now I have a blanket and a prayer.
Wolves followed us two nights on the road. Bigger than any wolves I've ever seen.
The folk here are kind enough, but kindness doesn't stretch forever. I can see it thinning.
I was a weaver in my village. Give me a loom and I'll earn my keep, I swear it.
They came out of the woods at night. Grey things, with too many joints. We just ran.
My husband stayed behind to hold the door. I keep looking down the road for him.
I sleep in a stable with three families. At least the horse doesn't snore. Much.
Someday I'll go back and plant barley again. Someday soon, gods willing.
A priest from Vel Morrath gave us bread on the road. I'll remember his face till I die.
Everything I own is in this sack. It's lighter than you'd think, a whole life.
Don't pity me, friend. I'm alive. Many from my village can't say the same.
We buried my father by the roadside under an elm. I hope someone tends the stone.
The children here throw stones at mine for the way they talk. Children can be cruel.
I heard Graymourne takes in our kind. But the road there is long and foggy.
You fight the things in the dark? Then you fight for us too. Thank you.
First our well went bad, then the crops, then the neighbours started vanishing in the night.
I counted the stars every night on the road. They were the only thing that stayed the same.
My daughter still laughs. I don't know how. I'm grateful every time I hear it.
They say there's work in the fields if we're willing. I'm willing. I'm always willing.
I left my mother's ring buried under the hearthstone. One day I'll dig it up again.
When the bells ring here at night, my boy screams. He thinks they've come for us again.
Bandits took our cart at the crossroads. Left us the mule, at least. Out of pity, I suppose.
Hunger is a patient thing. It sits beside you all day and never says a word.
I don't know these streets or their saints, but the walls are high, and that's enough.
We were twelve families when we set out. Five made it through the forest.
A kind woman here gave me a shawl. I've nothing to give back but my thanks.
I used to dream of travelling. Now I dream of standing still in one place forever.
My hands still shake. They shook the whole way here and never once stopped.
Tell me, is the north road clear? My sister's family was a day behind us.
Have I told you about the time I arm wrestled a troll? I won. Mostly. He let me.
Another round! No? Well, I'll just drink yours then, if you're not having it.
Oh, the maid of the mill had eyes like ale... no, wait, that's not how it goes.
I used to be an adventurer too, you know. Then I found the tavern. Much safer.
The floor keeps moving. Tell it to stop. It listens to strangers better than me.
I once met a daemon down the Mistgate. Bought it a drink. Nice fellow, terrible breath.
Don't marry, friend. Don't gamble either. Do drink, though. Drinking's the only honest vice.
My wife left me for a cooper. Said I was too fond of his barrels. Ha! Barrels.
I swear on my mother's grave. She's alive, mind you, but I swear on it anyway.
Sing with me! Ten tankards on the shelf, ten tankards... where did they all go?
You've got two faces. Both lovely. Which one of you should I be talking to?
I'm not drunk. I'm just tired, and the ale is helping me be tired properly.
Used to own a farm, three pigs and a fine hat. Now I own this stool. Mostly.
The barkeep says I've had enough. The barkeep's a liar and a very fine man.
Ashenreach ale tastes of coal smoke. Graymourne ale tastes of fish. This ale tastes of more.
I'll tell you a secret. The castle's not haunted. It's just very, very sad.
Had a dream last night that I was sober. Worst nightmare of my life.
I fought orcs, I did. Fifty of them. Or five. It was dark, and I was thirsty.
Lend us a copper, will you? I'll pay you back in stories. I've got thousands.
Every man in this tavern has a broken heart. Mine's just broken louder.
Why do spiders have eight legs? So they can run from me twice as fast!
My father drank, his father drank, and here I am, keeping up the family trade.
Oh, the mist rolls in and the mist rolls out, and nobody knows what it's about...
Shh. Listen. Can you hear that? That's the sound of my purse being empty.
I loved a girl once. She sold turnips. I still can't look at a turnip without weeping.
I've drunk in every tavern from here to Kethrys Spire. Got thrown out of all of them.
The trick to not falling over is to hold onto the wall. The wall's my best friend.
Here's to the heroes! Here's to the dead! Here's to whoever's paying for this!
My leg aches when it's going to rain. My head aches when it isn't. Fair's fair.
I'm going to stop drinking tomorrow. I've been saying so for eleven years now.
You're the one who goes below? Bring me back a bottle. Dungeon wine, the strongest you find.
Once I bet a bard I could sing louder than him. Lost my voice and my boots.
Ah, don't look at me like that. My mother looked at me like that. Same eyes, nearly.
Sit down, sit down. The night's young, and I'm old, and the ale's halfway decent.
